items.title: Joe Wilder Part 2 interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 12, 1998
items.q: I did the Haydn “Trumpet Concerto” a few times with the Municipal Concerts Orchestra in New York.

ctx.x: Here’s another hard question. Can you recall some of the most difficult playing situations you’ve been in, just from a trumpet standpoint? And did you get through them successfully?

A couple of times when I played with the Philharmonic, and it wasn’t difficult but I found it to be a little stressful because here you’re somebody who is not really generally playing in that idiom and now you’re in the middle of it and you’ve got to perform like everybody else, and I found that a little tensing. But it’s rewarding of course to do it, and I was very flattered, because how often does anybody who’s supposed to be a commercial or a jazz player get an opportunity to do something like that. It was…
The definition of a mistake is much clearer in that music. © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -13-
